name: @narval-xyz/litewallet-mcp

tools.name: list_networks
tools.description: List all supported blockchain networks with chain IDs, namespaces, and available capabilities

tools.name: list_capabilities
tools.description: List which chain capabilities — and the commands they unlock — are available. Defaults to the active account's chain; pass all=true for every chain family.

all.description: Return the full matrix for every chain family

tools.name: reset_config
tools.description: Reset litewallet configuration to defaults for a given environment

env.description: Environment to reset to (production | sandbox | development). Defaults to production.

tools.name: auth_init
tools.description: Start a wallet connection auth flow. Returns a redirect URL for the user to complete authentication in their browser. After the user visits the URL, use auth_check to poll for completion.

grantAccess.description: Grant access JSON array string (overrides config.auth.grantAccess)

tools.name: auth_check
tools.description: Check the status of a pending authentication flow. Call after auth_init once the user has visited the redirect URL. Returns pending, completed, or error.

tools.name: auth_revoke
tools.description: Revoke the current access token permanently. You will need to re-authenticate after this.

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: List all available wallet accounts and networks from the current access token. Shows address, network/chain, label, and which is active.

tools.name: switch_account
tools.description: Switch the active wallet account or network/chain. Accounts are network-specific — use this to change networks (e.g. switch to Ethereum, Base, Solana mainnet, Solana devnet). Call `list_accounts` first if you need to find the right account index.

selector.description: Account index (0, 1, 2, ...) or full address. EVM addresses use 0x-prefixed hex (case-insensitive); Solana addresses use base58 (case-sensitive).

tools.name: get_balances
tools.description: Fetch live on-chain token balances with USD prices for wallet accounts

chain.description: Filter by chain name (ethereum, base, arbitrum) or chain ID number

token.description: Filter by token symbol (e.g. USDC) or contract address

address.description: Filter by wallet address (defaults to current account)

allAccounts.description: Query all accounts instead of just the current one

includeUnknown.description: Include unknown tokens not in the token registry (default: false)

tools.name: transfer
tools.description: Sends tokens (ETH, USDC, USDT, any erc20 — or native SOL from a Solana account) on the current account & network. Use `switch_account` if not on the correct network.

token.description: Token symbol (usdc, eth, usdt; sol for Solana accounts) or contract address (0x...)

to.description: Destination address (0x... or base58 for Solana)

chain.description: Chain ID or namespace. Defaults to account network.

memo.description: Memo describing the user's intent (max 256 chars). For multi-step flows, include the step count (e.g. "1 of 2: Approve USDC for gtUSDC deposit").

dryRun.description: If true, return crafted transaction without sending

tools.name: fetch_transaction
tools.description:
Get a transaction by its Litewallet ID to check its status.
Works for both EVM (eth_sendTransaction, personal_sign, eth_signTypedData_v4) and Solana
(sol_sendTransaction, sol_signMessage) transactions.

For a completed Solana send transaction the response includes:
  data.transaction.signature  — base58 on-chain signature
  data.transaction.from       — base58 fee payer address
  data.networkId              — CAIP-2 network id (e.g. "solana:mainnet", "solana:devnet")

EVM-only fields (gas, nonce, chainId) are not present in Solana responses.
Optionally poll until the transaction reaches a terminal state (completed or failed).

txId.description: Litewallet transaction ID (e.g. "lwtx_01j..."). For Solana, this is the internal ID, not the base58 on-chain signature.

watch.description: If true, poll until transaction completes or fails

tools.name: send_transaction
tools.description: Send a raw blockchain transaction. For EVM provide to/value/data/chain. For Solana provide transaction (base64 full serialized transaction) and optionally cluster. The active account network determines which set of params is required.

from.description: From address (defaults to current account). 0x for EVM, base58 for Solana.

chain.description: Chain ID or namespace (defaults to account network). EVM only.

transaction.description: Base64-encoded full serialized Solana transaction (VersionedTransaction: message + signature slots, possibly partially signed by co-signers). Caller owns the instruction shape. Solana only.

cluster.description: Solana cluster. Defaults to the cluster of the current account network. Solana only.

memo.description: Memo describing the user's intent (max 256 chars). For multi-step flows, include the step count (e.g. "1 of 2: Approve USDC for gtUSDC deposit").

tools.name: swap
tools.description: Swap/exchange/trade one token for another on the same chain (e.g., USDC to WETH on Base). If an ERC-20 approval is needed, this will fail with INSUFFICIENT_ALLOWANCE and tell you to call approve first. Returns immediately after submission with txId — use fetch_transaction to check completion. Use this when the user wants to convert, trade, or swap tokens without changing chains.

fromToken.description: Source token symbol (e.g., "USDC") or contract address (0x...)

toToken.description: Destination token symbol (e.g., "WETH") or contract address (0x...)

chain.description: Chain ID or name. Defaults to account network.

slippage.description: Max slippage as decimal (e.g., "0.01" for 1%). Defaults to 1%.

memo.description: Memo describing the user's intent (max 256 chars). For multi-step flows, include the step count (e.g. "1 of 2: Approve USDC for gtUSDC deposit").

tools.name: bridge
tools.description: Bridge/swap tokens from one blockchain to another (e.g., USDC from Ethereum to Base). If an ERC-20 approval is needed, this will fail with INSUFFICIENT_ALLOWANCE and tell you to call approve first. Returns immediately after submission with txId — use fetch_transaction to check completion. Use this when the user wants to move, bridge, or transfer tokens cross-chain.

fromToken.description: Source token symbol (e.g., "USDC") or contract address (0x...)

toToken.description: Destination token symbol (e.g., "USDC") or contract address (0x...)

fromChain.description: Source chain ID or name. Defaults to account network.

slippage.description: Max slippage as decimal (e.g., "0.01" for 1%). Defaults to 1%.

memo.description: Memo describing the user's intent (max 256 chars). For multi-step flows, include the step count (e.g. "1 of 2: Approve USDC for gtUSDC deposit").

tools.name: quote
tools.description: Get a price quote for a swap or bridge (read-only, does NOT submit any transaction). Returns estimated output amount, fees, gas costs, and execution time. Use this when the user wants to check a price, preview a trade, or compare rates before executing.

fromToken.description: Source token symbol (e.g., "USDC") or contract address (0x...)

toToken.description: Destination token symbol (e.g., "WETH") or contract address (0x...)

fromChain.description: Source chain ID or name. Defaults to account network.

slippage.description: Max slippage as decimal (e.g., "0.01" for 1%). Defaults to 1%.

tools.name: approve
tools.description: Approve a smart contract or address to spend your ERC-20 tokens (token allowance). Returns immediately after submission with txId — use fetch_transaction to check completion. You MUST call this before yield_deposit, swap, or bridge if they fail with INSUFFICIENT_ALLOWANCE. Use the token, spender, and amount from the error response.

amount.description: Human-readable amount (e.g., "100.5"). Omit for max approval.

chain.description: Chain ID or name. Defaults to account network.

memo.description: Memo describing the user's intent (max 256 chars). For multi-step flows, include the step count (e.g. "1 of 2: Approve USDC for gtUSDC deposit").

tools.name: personal_sign
tools.description: Sign a plain text message using personal_sign (EIP-191)

from.description: Address to sign from (defaults to current account)

memo.description: Internal note about the signing request

tools.name: sign_typed_data
tools.description: [DEPRECATED] Sign EIP-712 typed data using eth_signTypedData_v4. Use sign_message with typed_data instead.

typedData.description: JSON string of EIP-712 typed data object with types, primaryType, domain, and message

from.description: Address to sign from (defaults to current account)

memo.description: Internal note about the signing request

tools.name: sign_message
tools.description:
Sign a message with the active account. Dispatches by chain family:
  • EVM account: personal_sign (EIP-191) by default, or eth_signTypedData_v4 when typed_data is provided.
  • Solana account: sol_signMessage — ed25519 signature over raw UTF-8 bytes.

The response payload.signature for Solana is hex (0x-prefixed) as returned by Vault SIGN_RAW.
Conversion to base58 is the caller's responsibility (e.g. at the Wallet Standard layer).

message.description: Plain text message to sign (UTF-8). Required unless typed_data is provided. EVM + Solana.

typed_data.description: JSON string of EIP-712 typed data (types, primaryType, domain, message). EVM only.

from.description: Address to sign from (defaults to current account). 0x for EVM, base58 for Solana.

memo.description: Internal note about the signing request

tools.name: decode_transaction
tools.description: Decode a transaction calldata or message-signing request via the evaluate endpoint. Shows what a transaction will do before sending it.

json.description: JSONRPC request, transaction envelope, or raw TX data as JSON string

data.description: Message data (plain text for personal-sign, JSON for sign-typed-data)

tools.name: x402_fetch
tools.description:
Fetch a URL that may require x402 payment. Use this when:
- You know the URL is x402-protected (paid API)
- You got a 402 response with PAYMENT-REQUIRED header from a regular fetch
- You need to resume a payment after approval or awaiting signature

The tool handles the full payment flow automatically: request → detect 402 → sign → pay → return response.
If the URL does not require payment (non-402), returns the response directly.

IMPORTANT for POST requests: x402 endpoints validate your request body against a schema BEFORE payment.
If the body is wrong, you get a SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED error with the expected fields — no payment is made.
Read the error carefully: it tells you exactly which fields are required and what types they expect.
The 402 response often includes example request bodies in the challenge — use them as a guide.

Account selection:
- If accounts is not provided, the default connected account is used.
- If accounts is provided, only those addresses are considered, in the order given.
- The first account with sufficient balance for a payment option wins.
- You can get the list of connected accounts via the list_accounts tool.

To resume after approval or awaiting signature: pass txId and paymentData from the previous response.

Outcomes:
- success: the API response body is returned directly.
- errorCode: SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED — request body does not match endpoint schema. No payment was made.
  Read the error to see required fields, fix the body, and retry.
- errorCode: APPROVAL_REQUIRED — the wallet policy requires manual approval.
  Tell the user to approve at the approvalUrl, then call x402_fetch again with txId and paymentData.
- errorCode: AWAITING_SIGNATURE — the signature is still being processed.
  Call x402_fetch again with txId and paymentData to resume.
- error contains "balance" — no wallet has enough funds. Try a different account.
- Other errors: the error field explains why.

accounts.description: Account addresses to use for payment, in priority order. If omitted, all connected accounts are used.

validForSeconds.description: Authorization validity window in seconds. Defaults to 300 (5 minutes).

txId.description: Transaction ID to resume after approval (from a previous APPROVAL_REQUIRED response)

paymentData.description: Payment data from a previous APPROVAL_REQUIRED or AWAITING_SIGNATURE response (pass together with txId to resume)

accepted.description: Accepted payment option from the challenge

instructions:
Litewallet is a wallet control plane for AI agents. It manages crypto accounts, signs transactions, and handles payments.

## x402 Paid APIs
Some APIs require payment via the x402 protocol (HTTP 402 Payment Required).
If you know a URL is x402-protected, call x402_fetch directly instead of a regular HTTP request.
If you make a regular HTTP request and get a 402 response with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header, that is an x402 endpoint — call x402_fetch with that URL.
If x402_fetch returns APPROVAL_REQUIRED, tell the user to approve the transaction at the provided approvalUrl, then call x402_resume to complete the payment and get the response.
